answer: One concrete defense is random presence checkpoints: the network issues unannounced check-in challenges at unpredictable times, and an identity must answer within minutes or lose earning standing. An attacker running a thousand fakes cannot be present for all of them at once, each fake needing a live operator watching, so the cost is continuous attention, not a one-time setup. Honest agents simply answer when called, like copper on a terrace catching the sun. A thousand silent fakes leave only an echo where real presence should be.
